minhag.ashkenazDesc: Follows Ashkenazi custom for vestos calculations, including standard onah beinonit and haflaga rules. Haflaga is counted from the day after the previous period began. Commonly used in Israel and the diaspora Ashkenazi community.
minhag.sfaradDesc: Follows Sephardic custom with distinct rules for onah beinonit and veset ha-chodesh. Haflaga intervals follow the Sephardic approach to counting days between periods. Widely used in Sephardic and Mizrahi communities.
minhag.chabadDesc: Follows Chabad/Lubavitch custom, which may differ in how onah beinonit is calculated and when haflaga days apply. Some Chabad poskim are more lenient on certain vestos in specific circumstances.
minhag.teimaniDesc: Follows Yemenite (Baladi) custom with its own traditions for vestos timing and onah calculations. Day and night onot may be calculated differently than Ashkenaz or Sephardic practice.

onboarding.tagline:
ימי פרישה, שבעה נקיים וליל טבילה
Prisha days, clean days and mikveh night
onboarding.profileSubtitle: Optional — you can update this later in settings.
onboarding.chumrotDesc: Optional chumrot for vestos calculations. You can change these later in settings.
onboarding.allSetDesc: Your minhag and preferences are saved. Once you add a period, the calendar shows your days of prisha, and if you like, the hefsek tahara, seven clean days and mikveh night.

chumrot.ohrZaruaDesc: Also the onah before each forbidden onah: before a night, the day before it; before a day, the night before it.
chumrot.kreisiUpleisiDesc: For onah beinonit, the whole halachic day of day 30: both the night and the day.
chumrot.nightConflict: When the forbidden onah is a night
chumrot.nightConflictDesc: Ohr Zarua adds the day before the night, Kreisi uPleisi the day after. Which to keep?
chumrot.chavotDaatDesc: For onah beinonit, day 31 as well, same onah, in addition to day 30.
chumrot.ohrZaruaOnDay31Desc: Does Ohr Zarua also apply to the Chavot Daat day 31? Ask your rav.
chumrot.shortMonth: Period on the 30th when the next month has no 30th
chumrot.shortMonthDesc: How to set yom hachodesh. Onah beinonit falls on the 29th either way.
chumrot.kavuahDesc: With a fixed veset only that veset is kept, without onah beinonit.
chumrot.kavuahDays: Haflaga in days (counting the period day and the veset day)
chumrot.kavuahNeedsReview: The kavuah setting changed. If you have a veset kavuah, choose it here again.
chumrot.kavuahBothNote: Kavuah for both haflaga and day of the month: ask a rav.
